look_here_first: Start low on the plant, near the lowest nodes and leaf litter. The strange brown-purple flower has no ordinary petal whorl: the showy structure is a bent, tubular petaloid calyx/perianth. Then confirm the variable lanceolate-to-cordate leaves and the nearly spherical dry capsule.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: rhizomatous perennial herb, often inconspicuous in woodland litter

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves variable from lanceolate to heart-shaped

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers solitary on slender scaly peduncles from low nodes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: petals absent; showy structure is a tubular S-shaped petaloid calyx/perianth

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perianth brownish purple, enlarged basally and distally, with an unevenly three-lobed tip

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dry nearly spherical capsule with numerous seeds

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Use A. serpentaria to teach that Aristolochia's bizarre flower is not a normal corolla. The perianth/calyx tube, inferior ovary, low flower position and capsule matter more than leaf shape alone.

key_traits.label: Ecology
key_traits.text: Moist to mesic woodland and shaded calcareous sites in Central Texas; larval host for pipevine swallowtail.
